title: Sell Mineral Rights in Montoursville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Montoursville, PA | Lycoming County
metaDescription: Montoursville, PA mineral owners near Williamsport: we buy Lycoming County dry-gas Marcellus interests directly, no listing, no broker fees.
heroLead: Montoursville sits just east of Williamsport where the Loyalsock Creek meets the Susquehanna, close enough to the county seat that a lot of local mineral owners have their deeds recorded just a few miles from where they live.
intro: Lycoming County's Marcellus development reaches right up to Montoursville's edges, with operators active throughout the surrounding townships for over a decade. If you own land here, or inherited a share from family land nearby, your interest is likely tied to one of the large pooled units that cover much of this part of the county.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Montoursville directly. We're upfront about our process: we review your title and production data first, then explain our offer in plain terms.

sections.heading: Close to Williamsport, Deep in the Play
paragraphs: Being near the county seat doesn't change the geology, Montoursville sits well within Lycoming County's productive dry-gas Marcellus fairway, and operators have treated this area as core acreage since the early years of development.

Wells here typically follow the standard Marcellus decline pattern, a strong first year or two followed by a longer, steadier tail. If your interest has been producing for several years, we'll look at that full arc rather than a single recent statement.

sections.heading: Title Research Close to Home
paragraphs: Because the Lycoming County Recorder of Deeds is right in Williamsport, records for Montoursville-area parcels are generally well organized, which can make title research move faster than in more rural corners of the county.
That said, we still verify every link in the chain of title carefully, since even well-documented parcels can have inheritance or reservation issues worth catching before a sale.

sections.heading: Reading Your Lease's Deduction Clause
paragraphs: We'll review your lease's specific language on post-production costs with you, since that clause, more than almost anything else, determines how much of your gross production value actually reaches your account.

faqs.question: Does being close to Williamsport change how you value my interest?
faqs.answer: No, value is driven by your decimal interest, the well's production, and lease terms, not proximity to the county seat, though it can make records easier to research.

faqs.question: What's the difference between gross and net royalty on my statement?
faqs.answer: Gross reflects total production value before deductions; net is what actually reaches you after gathering, compression, and other post-production costs are subtracted. We'll walk through both with you.

faqs.question: How quickly can you review my documents?
faqs.answer: Most initial reviews take about a week once we have your deed and any lease or royalty paperwork you can share.
